too_consistent.title: Too Consistent to Detect: A Study of Self-Consistent Errors in LLMs
too_consistent.location: Table 2, PDF page 4 (proceedings page 4758); subset construction in Section 3.1, PDF page 3
too_consistent.verification: Values and the two distinct cross-model rows checked against extracted PDF text and rendered original Table 2.

recall.setting: Zero-shot, one-hop, closed-book factual QA; concise answers without explicit chain-of-thought; greedy decoding; fact-level train-test deduplication.
notes: The Base row in Table 1 means the starting instruction-tuned model before this factual RL training, not a pretrained base checkpoint. This differs from base model in BaseCal.
The RL row uses GRPO with binary semantic-correctness rewards. Values are accuracies in percent; changes should be reported in percentage points unless explicitly computed as relative changes.
SimpleQA is intentionally included: the paper reports no meaningful improvement there. Do not imply that all models and benchmarks improve.
These accuracy results alone do not prove knowledge storage or its absence. The paper uses separate accessibility and pass@k analyses to study the mechanism.

self_consistent_errors.setting: Detection of errors in greedy answers; comparison of CE and IE evaluation subsets as constructed in Section 3.1.
notes: CE means a greedy wrong answer whose 15 stochastic samples are all semantically equivalent to it; IE contains other incorrect answers.

CE and IE are different subsets, not two evaluation protocols on identical questions. The paper matches negative example counts and positive example counts for supervised training, controlling training-data volume.
AUROC measures correct-versus-incorrect discrimination, not confidence calibration or response accuracy. Scores are fractions on a 0-to-1 scale; 0.5 is chance discrimination.
Probe (ID) is trained and evaluated in-domain. Probe + cross-model uses the cross-model row immediately below Probe (ID), not the distinct OOD cross-model row.
For this generator, the external verifier is Qwen2.5-14B. The cross-model method trains supervised probes on hidden states from both models; it is not training-free.
